title: Dust mopping hard floors and removing dry soil
audience: Cleaners who clear dry soil off hard floors before wet cleaning, in offices, shared buildings and homes.
learningOutcomes: Describe the parts of a dust mop and fit or change a head without contaminating the clean side.
Dust mop a room in controlled passes, gathering dust without lifting it back into the air.
Clean the dust mop's head after use and return it to storage ready for the next job.

instruction.heading: Why dust mopping comes before wet cleaning
instruction.body: Dry soil such as grit, hair and crumbs is abrasive when it is pushed around on a wet floor. Removing it first means the wet clean lifts only the film and marks, not grit that scratches the surface. Dust mopping is the standard first pass for hard floors, and it should be done before any mop water is used.

instruction.heading: Heads, fastenings and the clean side
instruction.body: Dust mop heads fasten to the frame in several ways: a zip, ties, a slot pocket, snaps, or a breakaway fitting. The head should be changed when it is full of soil or has lost its ability to hold dust. For a zip-fastened head, open the zip, draw the frame out of the soiled head, and bag that head for laundering. Thread the frame into a fresh head and close the zip. For a flat-style dust pad, the pad is peeled from the holder and a new one is pressed on, so the hook-and-loop backing grips. Keep the clean head in a clean bag until it is needed.

instruction.heading: The dust mopping pass
instruction.body: Remove floor mats before you start. Start in a corner and keep the head on the floor the whole time. Walk backwards with an even, steady push, moving across the room in overlapping passes. Each pass should be a few centimetres over the previous one so no strip is missed. Push the dust into a pile near the centre of the room. Lift the head only at the end to shake it lightly into the pile, then sweep the pile into a dust pan with a broom and empty it into the bin. Work carefully: lifting the head and swinging it up throws dust back into the air.

instruction.heading: Cleaning the head after the job
instruction.body: Take the dust mop back to the cleaning cupboard before cleaning it. Work a stiff bristle brush through the head above a bin so the dust drops in. A backpack vacuum can draw the dust out instead. Do not shake a dirty head in an occupied area. Once clean, hang or store the head so that it cannot touch the floor, and let it dry if it has been damp.

procedure: Put on gloves and remove mats and loose items from the floor.
Place a wet floor sign by the room entrance if the floor is going to be wet cleaned straight after.
Start in a corner and walk backwards in even, overlapping passes, keeping the head on the floor.
Push dust toward the centre of the room, then lift the head only to shake it lightly into the pile.
Sweep the pile into a dust pan with a broom and empty it into the bin.
Return the dust mop to storage and clean the head with a bristle brush above a bin, or with a backpack vacuum.
Store the head clean and dry, away from the floor.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner in a corridor lifts the dust mop high at the end of each pass and swings it back to the start, and the dust hangs in the air for several minutes.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is wrong with the technique, and how should the corridor be done?
workedExamples.reasoning: Lifting and swinging the head throws dust into the air and back onto cleaned areas. Keep the head on the floor, use even overlapping passes, and gather the dust into a pile to be collected at the end. Pause the work if a person is nearby until the air has settled.

workedExamples.situation: A dust mop's head is visibly full of grit and hair after sweeping a busy office corridor, and the cleaner wants to use it on the next room.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should the head be used again, and what is the right step?
workedExamples.reasoning: A full head will spread soil rather than collect it. Clean or change the head before the next room, and place the dirty head in a bag for laundering if it cannot be cleaned on site.

equipmentAndPpe: Dust mop frame with a clean head, or a flat-style dust pad holder with a clean pad.
Trash bin and a plastic bag for dirty heads.
Back-pack vacuum, where available, for cleaning heads.

commonErrors.error: Lifting the head off the floor and swinging it, which throws dust back into the air.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the head on the floor and push in steady passes, lifting only to shake at the end.

commonErrors.error: Using a full or dirty head to finish a room.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the head before each room, and clean or change it when it is full.

commonErrors.error: Pushing dust into corners and under furniture without collecting it.
commonErrors.prevention: Gather the dust toward the centre of the room, then sweep the pile up.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Wear gloves when handling a dirty head, as it can hold grit, sharp debris and food residue.
Keep the dust mop and broom clear of walkways. Set a wet floor sign if the floor is about to be mopped.

qualityStandard: The floor is free of visible dry soil, grit and hair after the pass.
The dust is gathered into a pile and removed, not left in corners or under furniture.
The dust mop's head is clean and dry before storage.
No dust cloud is raised during the pass.
documentationEvidence: Job record showing the floor was dust mopped, with the area and time.
Note of any head that was torn, worn, or unable to be cleaned, so it can be replaced.
summary: Dust mop before any wet clean, so grit does not scratch the floor.
Keep the head on the floor and make even overlapping passes.
Gather the dust into a pile and collect it rather than lifting it.
Clean the head after each job and store it clean and off the floor.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is dry soil removed before a wet clean?
options: Because mop water works only on dry floors and it will not clean a dirty floor
So that grit is not dragged across the floor by the wet mop and does not scratch it
So that the wet floor sign is not needed because the floor is never wet

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the correct way to move the dust mop across a floor?
options: Lift the head at the end of each pass and swing it back to the start
Use fast, short strokes that do not overlap
Keep the head on the floor and make even, overlapping passes

knowledgeChecks.question: When should a dust mop's head be washed or replaced?
options: When it is full or no longer holds dust, before it is used on another room
Only at the far end of the week and only if the room is quiet
Only if a client asks for it to be changed and never on the same day
